title: Protocol for intracellular and extracellular metabolite detection in human embryonic stem cells
protocol: Thaw one bottle of Matrigel on ice for 12–24 hours the day before the experiment.
Pre-chill empty 2-mL Eppendorf tubes in -80°C refrigerator.
Aliquot 2 mg of Matrigel into each pre-chilled 2-mL Eppendorf tube.
Freeze aliquoted Matrigel immediately at -80°C.
Store aliquoted Matrigel at -80°C.
Pre-chill DMEM/F12 at 4°C for at least 1 hour.
Dilute 2 mg of aliquoted Matrigel in 36 mL cold DMEM/F12.
Aliquot 1 mL of diluted Matrigel into each well of a 6-well plate.
Gently shake the plate to cover the whole surface without air bubbles.
Leave the plate in a 37°C incubator for at least 30 minutes before use.
Take a Matrigel-coated 6-well plate out of storage if prepared earlier and stored at 4°C.
Aspirate medium from the wells you plan to use.
Add 2 mL/well E8 medium containing 10 μM Y-27632.
Prepare a 37°C water bath.
Take the cryotube with frozen cell stock out of liquid nitrogen tank and put it directly in the 37°C water bath.
Transfer cells into a 15-mL conical tube.
Drop-wise add 10 mL E8 medium + 10 μM Y-27632 while mixing continuously.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of E8 + 10 μM Y-27632.
Seed the resuspended cells into wells of Matrigel-coated plates containing E8.
Change the medium daily by aspirating spent medium and adding 2 mL fresh E8.
Passage human ES/iPS cells when they reach 60–70% confluence or after 5–6 days if survival is poor.
Aspirate the remaining medium from Matrigel-coated plates.
Rinse cells twice with 1 mL DPBS-EDTA solution per well without incubation.
Add 1 mL DPBS-EDTA solution to each well and incubate at 37°C for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the DPBS-EDTA solution.
Harvest cells with 1 mL of E8 medium + 5 μM Y-27632 by pipetting up and down.
Seed the cell suspension into Matrigel-coated plates containing E8 medium and 5 μM Y-27632.
Gently shake the plate until cells are evenly distributed.
Place the plate in a 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
Change the medium to 2 mL/well E8 medium without ROCK inhibitor the next day.
Aspirate the spent medium and add 2 mL fresh E8 medium for each well of a 6-well plate.
Change medium on cells reaching ∼80% confluence.
Add 2 mL fresh E8 medium per well for 6-well plates.
Add appropriate treatments as required by the experiment design.
Monitor cell confluence daily under microscope to avoid over-confluence.
Count cells from three wells of each condition when ready for metabolic analysis.
Aspirate the medium from the wells.
Add 500 μL/well of TrypLE Select.
Incubate in a 37°C environment for 5 minutes.
Neutralize with 500 μL of 5% FBS in DMEM/F12.
Determine the cell count using a hemocytometer or flow cytometer.
Collect medium and extract with medium extraction solution when cells are ready.
Transfer 1 mL culture medium from each well to a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Spin at 1,000 x g for 5 minutes.
Transfer 100 μL of the supernatant into a new 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Add 900 μL medium extraction solution and vortex.
Spin at 18,000 × g at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Take 200 μL of supernatant for LC-MS analysis.
Prepare 0.9% saline on ice along with labeled tubes.
Ensure cell scrapers are pre-chilled at -80°C.
Make sure the cell extraction solution is also pre-chilled at -80°C.
Keep the cell extraction solution in -80°C until use.
Prepare two bottles of cell extraction solution.
Take one bottle out of the freezer for use with one plate and put it back immediately after use.
Use the other bottle for the next plate to minimize time at room temperature (15°C–30°C).
Perform the rinse quickly to avoid interference with results.
Rinse with saline to remove residual medium and floating cell debris.
Consider that washing cells with saline could decrease signal intensities of metabolites.
Rinse cells with 1 mL/well of ice-cold 0.9% saline twice.
Aspirate the saline from the wells.
Add 500 μL/well of cold cell extraction solution kept at −80°C.
Scrape off the cells using a cell scraper and transfer the suspension into a labeled, pre-chilled 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube (Tube 1).
Put the tubes on ice.
Wash each well with 100 μL of cell extraction solution and combine it into Tube 1.
Vortex each sample thoroughly.
Centrifuge the samples at 18,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5-mL tube (Tube 2).
Put the tubes on ice.
Vortex Tube 2 and put it back on ice.
Transfer 200 μL of extract into a sample vial for LC-MS analysis.
Put Milli-Q water and labeled glass vials on ice.
Rinse cells with 1 mL/well ice-cold 0.9% saline twice.
Aspirate the saline.
Add 250 μL/well −80°C methanol followed by adding 100 μL/well ice-cold Milli-Q water to the cells.
Scrape off cells and transfer the suspension into glass vials.
Put vials on ice.
Add 250 μL/vial −80°C chloroform containing 1 μg/mL heptadecanoate and 1 μg/mL coprostan-3-ol to each vial.
Vortex the mixture.
Centrifuge at 18,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove the upper hydrophilic phase from the centrifuged mixture.
Push aside the protein pellet at the interface carefully using a fresh tip.
Collect the hydrophobic phase with a fresh tip until reaching the interface.
Transfer the collected hydrophobic phase into a new glass vial.
Evaporate under nitrogen gas until dry.
Re-dissolve the residue in 100 μL 2:1 chloroform/methanol (v/v) for LC-MS analysis.
Decant supernatant and add 200 μL methanol to the protein pellet.
Vigorously vortex the mixture.
Centrifuge the sample at 18,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant into waste.
Let the protein pellet dry by placing the tube upside down on a Kimwipe in a biological safety cabinet for 5 min.
Dissolve the protein pellet with 400 μL protein denaturing solution.
Dilute bovine serum albumin standard to a series of concentrations in 1X PBS, typically from 0.1 to 1 mg/mL, to construct a standard curve.
Prepare the working reagent as instructed by the BCA kit manual.
Mix diluted samples or BSA standards with the working reagent in a 96-well microplate.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 30 min.
Check absorptance at 562 nm using a spectrophotometer.
Use the standard curve to determine the protein concentration of each sample.
Calibrate the mass spectrometer following manufacturer’s recommendation.
Use IntelliStart software to automatically tune and mass calibrate the instrument.
Ensure mobile phases and system wash solution are sufficient.
Install the UPLC column.
Purge the system with mobile phases at 4 mL/min for 4 min.
Equilibrate the column with initial gradient and flow rate until delta pressure is below 30 psi.
Check LC and MS performance.
Record the column pressure after equilibration.
Wash the column as instructed if abnormal column pressure increase happens.
Use an Amide column (Acquity UPLC BEH amide column, 2.1 × 100 mm, 1.7 μm) for separation.
Prepare acetonitrile with 0.1% formic acid as mobile phase A.
Prepare water with 0.1% formic acid as mobile phase B.
Apply the gradient settings listed in Table 5.
Use LC-MS/MS conditions and parameters displayed in Table 6 for quantification.
Generate representative chromatograms as shown in Figure 6.
Prepare fresh mobile phases before running LC-MS.
Degass mobile phases by ultrasonic bathing for 15 minutes.
Name the compound and select criteria for peak selection and response types.
Select “Process Samples” function in TargetLynx.
Set sample range and process method.
Review chromatogram showing peak integration using the process method.
Open chromatogram of standards, select channel of target compound, and set retention time range.
Right drag to select a range of retention time on the chromatogram.
Record MRM information and time range automatically in TargetLynx XS Method Editor.
Set nearest peak or largest peak within the time range as the target.
Choose peak area or peak height as response type.
Integrate multiple compound settings into one TargetLynx method.
Save edited method for future data processing.
Reduce injection volume until overlapping peaks are separated for metabolites with overlapping peaks.
Review results to verify correct peak finding and integration.
Modify TargetLynx Method if necessary.
Manually choose and integrate the peaks if needed.
Save the experimental results for further analysis.
Normalize peak responses from TargetLynx by internal control levels.
Normalize peak responses using cell number as a reference.
Normalize peak responses based on protein level measurements.
Calculate the average cell count ratio of treated wells to control wells.
Record protein concentration values for both control and treatment groups.
